notes.meaning: Paul compares our earthly bodies to tents, which are flimsy shelters that easily wear out and fall apart. In contrast, God has prepared an eternal resurrection body for believers in heaven that will never decay. Christians know with full confidence that physical death is not the end, but a doorway to a lasting home from God.

While living in these physical bodies, believers experience pain, weakness, and sorrow, causing them to groan. This groaning is not just sadness over earthly trouble, but an eager yearning to receive a heavenly, glorified body. God has placed within His people a deep longing for their final home.

Being clothed describes entering the next life with a glorious resurrection body rather than existing as a bare, disembodied spirit. Paul rejects the idea that being completely without a physical form is the best state, because God made humans to have bodies. Believers who are clothed in Christ and His righteousness will never be found bare or exposed before God.

Life in our mortal body brings heavy burdens from suffering and the struggle with sin. Christians do not want to die simply to escape pain, but to have their mortal weaknesses swallowed up and replaced by eternal life. The goal of faith is not to throw the body away, but to see it completely renewed and filled with endless life.

God Himself made believers for this very goal of sharing eternal life with Him. As a guarantee, He gave the Holy Spirit to dwell in our hearts right now. This gift of the Spirit acts like a down payment, assuring believers that God will finish what He started and bring them to full glory.

Knowing what God has promised gives believers steady courage in every trial. As long as Christians dwell in earthly bodies, they live like travelers far away from their true home with Christ. While the Lord is present with His people by His Spirit, they do not yet see Him face-to-face.

In this life, Christians guide their daily conduct by trusting God's promises rather than relying on what their physical eyes can see. Faith acts on the reality of eternal things that are currently invisible. Full sight belongs to the future world, where believers will finally see God openly.

Believers face death with confidence because leaving this earthly body means immediately being at home with Christ. The joy of a Christian is not delayed into an unconscious sleep, but begins the moment they enter the Lord's presence. Being with Jesus is what truly makes heaven home.

Because believers look forward to being with Christ, their greatest ambition is to live in a way that pleases Him. This holy aim guides their choices whether they are living on earth or present in heaven. Love for the Lord drives them to seek His approval every single day.

Every person will stand before Christ's judgment seat to give an account of what they did during earthly life. Jesus will openly evaluate all choices, giving each person what is fitting for either good or bad deeds. For believers, this evaluation does not threaten their pardon, but brings a gracious reward for faithful service.

differ.view: Teach that this judgment for Christians concerns only rewards for faithful service, with worthless works burned away and no threat of punishment for sin.

notes.meaning: Because Paul knows the solemn awe and reverence due to Christ as Judge, he works hard to convince people to trust the gospel. He does not frighten people with harsh threats, but gently urges them to turn to God. Paul's pure motives are clear to God, and he hopes the Corinthians recognize his sincerity as well.

Paul is not trying to boast or win personal praise by defending his work. Instead, he gives the Corinthian believers good reasons to stand up for him against critics. These rival teachers cared only about flashy outward appearances, rather than genuine devotion in the heart.

If Paul's passionate zeal for Christ made critics claim he had lost his mind, that intense devotion was directed toward God's glory. When he spoke calmly and carefully, it was for the instruction and benefit of the church. In every situation, his only aim was to honor God and build up other people.

The great love that Christ showed by dying for sinners holds Paul together and drives his entire life. Because Jesus died in the place of all, all are recognized as having been spiritually dead without Him. His death on the cross counted for all who belong to Him, freeing them from the power of death.

differ.view: Teach that Christ died effectively as the legal head and substitute specifically for all the elect, who died in Him.
Teach that Christ died for every human being without exception, proving that all people were spiritually dead and that salvation is available to everyone.

notes.meaning: Jesus died and rose again so that those who receive spiritual life would stop living selfishly for their own desires. Believers now belong to their Redeemer like servants bought by a master. Their time, talents, and energy are meant to honor the One who gave His life to rescue them.

Christians no longer evaluate other people by worldly standards like race, wealth, social rank, or human talent. Paul once viewed the promised Messiah this way too, expecting an earthly political ruler. After meeting the risen Jesus, Paul abandoned that worldly viewpoint and now sees Christ and all people through spiritual eyes.

When a person is joined to Christ by faith, God's power transforms them into a new creation. Their old worldly desires, sinful habits, and mistaken ideas begin to fade away. God gives them a new heart, new affections, and a completely fresh way of looking at life.

differ.view: Emphasize that the new creation involves an actual moral change in the believer's heart, producing inward holiness and freedom from sin.
Emphasize that being a new creation begins with a believer's spiritual rebirth and legal union with Christ, which then works itself out in renewed living.

notes.meaning: The entire work of making people new begins with God and depends on His grace. Sin created a deep rift between God and humanity, but God took the initiative to restore peace through Jesus. He then gave the apostles and ministers the task of announcing this reconciliation to the world.

In Jesus Christ, God was actively at work making peace with sinful humanity. Instead of holding people's sins against them and demanding full payment, He freely offers pardon because Christ bore the cost. God has entrusted the message of this free forgiveness to His messengers to share with all people.

Ministers serve as royal ambassadors sent by Jesus to speak on His behalf to the world. It is as though God Himself is pleading with sinners through human voices. The ambassadors urge all people to lay down their rebellion, accept God's offered peace, and enter into friendship with Him.

Jesus was completely pure and never committed any sin in thought, word, or deed. Yet God treated Him on the cross as the sin-bearer for humanity, placing the penalty for human guilt upon Him. In return, God gives believers the righteousness of Christ, accepting them as righteous in His sight.

differ.view: Teach that this verse shows double imputation, where our sin was legally credited to Christ and His perfect righteousness is credited to our account by faith alone.
Teach that Christ was made a sin-offering so that His righteousness might be both credited to us and planted inside us to produce actual holiness of life.
